openings.claim: Cork-padded bolted strips may retain either plate and permit gloved screwdriver release.
openings.delta: Replace magnetic dependence with screw-loaded friction through existing slots; drill supplied strips only.
openings.prediction: Against magnetic retention, equal clamp settings should reduce substitution sensitivity. Spare displacement above 1 mm or service above sixty seconds defeats the proposal; unknown preload and stroke loads prevent confidence.
openings.probe: Check M4 slot fit, support, clearance and screwdriver access first. Fabricate only if compliant; measure original and spare displacement over twenty strokes and time unmarked-edge removal/return, using gloves for the final spare check.
assumptions: Compliant mounting geometry and sufficient strip stiffness/preload exist.

openings.claim: A mechanically bounded pocket with a pivoting keeper may retain the plate without relying primarily on pad friction.
openings.delta: Bend supplied strips with pliers into opposing contact stops around unmarked regions; mount through existing slots. A drilled strip pivots on a supplied bolt to open the pocket, then overlaps an unmarked face to prevent lift.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival R1 relies on preload/friction. Under comparable safe pulls, a pocket should stop movement at its measured gap while R1 may continue slipping; neither behavior is observed. Magnetic differences should matter little. Gap above 1 mm, keeper lift, or slow gloved access defeats R2.
openings.probe: Before bending, check whether four strips and six bolts can provide opposing stops, lift restraint and accessible opening entirely outside clearance and working edge. If possible, reuse the same stock for a second configuration; mark references and compare displacement and service timing against R1. Optional scale pulls stop at 10 N; record arrested movement versus progressive slip without claiming stroke-load equivalence.
assumptions: Slot geometry supports a bounded pocket; strips are bendable and keeper access suits gloves.

assessment: Both are probes. Preserve every constraint. Share eighty fabrication minutes and twenty observation minutes; maximum two configurations, three runs and three service checks each. Final runs use the spare and gloved removal. Unknown stroke duration, geometry and ruler resolution may prevent informative completion; report that uncertainty rather than treat caps as feasibility.

lineage.reason: Preserves the incumbent clamp mechanism and acceptance commitments.
